findings.detail: If the snapshot launcher disappears or becomes invalid after the initial verification, uv or Python can fail with status 1 or 2 before Codex starts. This handler terminates only for 78, so it prints codex_status and permits the backend fallback despite the snapshot failure. A write-free handler probe confirmed that statuses 1 and 2 reach continuation with exit 0. The log retains diagnostics, but the status misclassifies the failure. The shared trim consumers inherit this behavior, which remains an instance of the recorded verification-failure fallback mechanism.
findings.fix: Before permitting fallback after a nonzero launch, reverify the pinned snapshot and terminate if verification fails. Add cases where the launcher disappears or becomes invalid between preverification and exec, then regenerate the trim reference copies.
findings.title: Uncited: Launcher startup failures can still enter the backend fallback.

strengths: Bash verification guards explicitly stop even when conditional sourcing disables errexit.
Evidence consumers report missing or mismatched producer provenance.
Snapshot creation refuses existing destinations and preserves failure diagnostics.
summary: Reviewed all 198 membership paths and their committed diffs, including shared copies and evidence fixtures. Inspection and a write-free handler probe identified one Important fallback defect; the full suite was not run. stopped: recurring defect.
